title: Ownership of the models and the function-node runtime: library, orchestrator, engine

settlements.topic: One owner for the org chart models, ChartChange, the closed base classes and the write gate
settlements.decision: The library (WPs L1 and L2) is the only owner of the chart models and the write gate: Value, Record, Gate/GATE/Checked/GateError, OrgNode, OrgEdge, OrgChart, NewNode, the five ops, ChartChangeRequest, ChartChange (one family 'chart_change' with kinds reuse, add, rearrange), ChartChangeResult, LinkPlan, apply_change, carry_links, slug_id. The orchestrator defines none of them; it owns the SQL tables, the approval policy (classify) and its extra rules. Rulings, one by one. (1) Base and gate: only Value/Record and GATE.check; no Closed base, no gate() function, no orchestrator copy of base.py or org_chart.py; every class in orchestrator/models.py (wire models, RunEvent variants, Event) derives from Value. (2) OrgNode keeps id, kind, name, purpose, functions, added_in; parent_id, position, state, merged_into, keywords and slug are not model fields. Wire ChartView.nodes[] = {id, kind, name, purpose, parent_id, position}: parent_id is read from OrgChart.edges and position is the index among siblings in OrgChart.nodes order (org_edges.position stays a projection written by ChartStore.apply). (3) A merged-away division leaves the chart; ChartChangeResult.aliases is projected into org_nodes as retired rows (state 'archived', merged_into) used only for history and the never-reuse-an-id guard; no archived node ever enters OrgChart or Node. (4) revision is the model field; the wire keeps the name version (= revision, and GraphView.chart_version). (5) Chart node ids are assigned by code: the model sends ref placeholders such as $web and ChartStore injects new_id = slug_id with taken widened by every id ever stored in org_nodes plus 'root'; the checks bad_id and retired_id can no longer fire and are deleted. (6) One class with three kinds: 'ChartReuse/ChartAdd/ChartRearrange' in the orchestrator text mean ChartChange of kind reuse, add, rearrange; the stage B reply class is ChartChangeRequest; the limit is 8 ops per change, not 50. (7) Violation codes are the library's (C1 to C12) plus reuse_candidate, busy, bad_assignment, not_plain; duplicate_id and unknown_parent do not exist (use unknown_node). (8) Tables: org_charts and chart_changes (orchestrator 4.1) are the only chart DDL; the library's org_changes DDL is dropped. (9) Wiring: orchestrator/db.py provides StoreContext, a GateContext bound to the open Tx (families node, atom, org_chart, department), and every store passes it as ctx; the AST test test_lib_write_paths scans an explicit list (tests/library/write_paths.txt) because the orchestrator stores are not named store*.py.
settlements.why: Rule 4 of the decision order: every concept has exactly one owner. Library section 4 was prototyped (a 300-step random walk keeps ids, aliases and function ids) and orchestrator 1.3 already adopts it, so only the residual differences above remain. Code-assigned ids end the invent-collide-retry loop and make the retired-id guard unreachable. A glob 'sutra_app/**/store*.py' matches none of the orchestrator files, so the write-path test would have scanned nothing.
settlements.rejected: A parallel chart model, Closed base or gate() inside the orchestrator (two charts that can drift); archived, merged_into, position or keywords as OrgNode fields (history and order are projections); model-chosen ids with bad_id/retired_id retries; a second DDL for the change log.

settlements.topic: Graph vocabulary: node ids, the step node key and the edge kinds
settlements.decision: Stored and wire ids are the library's: a chart node keeps its chart id (root, sales, leads), a function node is '<dept>.<fn>' (types.function_node_id), a step node is 's-' + the first 10 hex digits of sha1('<task_id>:<step_ref>'). The prefixes n:, f:, s: and the id pattern org_<12 hex> are dead. The step node key is (task_id, step_ref): the library StructuralNode fields workflow_id and step_id are renamed task_id and step_ref, and step_ref is 'task' (the department's task step), 'W-<n>' (a J2 builder) or 'team:<role>' (a J2 persona). There is one list of seven edge kinds in GraphEdge.kind: contains, has_function, has_step, handoff, step, speaks_to, depends_on. Stored in graph_edges: handoff, step, speaks_to, depends_on (each with a source record). Derived on read and never stored: contains (from the chart), has_function (a function node to its department), has_step (a step to its parent). check_graph runs on stored plus derived edges, so G4 holds by construction and invariant I7 stays. The fields reads, rework and handoff[] of the step event are event names only: a read becomes a depends_on edge labelled 'reads', a rework a depends_on edge labelled 'revises', a hand-off a handoff edge; 'reads' and 'rework' are not edge kinds anywhere.
settlements.why: One vocabulary from J2's map through the library to the UI (ORCH-D6). The tree has one writer (the chart), so no stored copy can drift. The key (task_id, step_ref) also names builder and persona steps that have no assignment id. J2's rule 'no line without a record' needs a source only on stored edges.
settlements.rejected: Prefixed ids n:/f:/s: and org_<hex> with a mapping layer at the API edge; a stored contains edge (a second chart); reads and rework as edge kinds; workflow_id/step_id keyed to a TaskWorkflow (it cannot name a W-n builder); a UI-only 'feeds' kind.

settlements.topic: L-1: Node.state against J2's box results, the outcome column and the node's atom list
settlements.decision: Node.state is one field holding J2's nine map/1 statuses: idle, running, waiting, waiting_on_you, fault, filed, done_unchecked, left_open, not_made. Validators: a function node uses only the first five (J2's function states); root, department and division use idle, running, waiting_on_you, fault; a step node may use all nine. The orchestrator's outcome column, its CHECK, the value 'archived' and the rule 'wire status = outcome else state' are removed: GraphNodeOut.status = Node.state. A merged-away division's graph node is deleted (S2-models-11), so no node state is 'archived'. Node gains detail: S(0,300) = '' (J2's one-line node detail) so every column the store indexes is a projection of Checked.model. FunctionNode drops the unbounded atoms list (the 501st atom would fail validation): it keeps open_atom: AtomId? and gains atom_count: int>=0; the list of atoms is the atoms table, and check G6 leaves check_graph because the unique index one_open_atom_per_node enforces it.
settlements.why: J2's map/1 has one status field with nine words (docs/map-schema.md, Statuses), so one field keeps J2 behaviour and removes a precedence rule. A column the model cannot produce breaks the library rule that projections are computed from Checked.model. The capped atoms list was a latent crash at the 501st atom of a long-lived department.
settlements.rejected: A separate outcome field or column (two fields with a precedence rule, and the stored body would not hold the truth); a five-word state with a wire-only mapping; 'archived' as a node state; keeping atoms: [AtomId]<=500.

settlements.topic: L-2: ChartChangeRequest.ops as a union or a flat op class, and the live check
settlements.decision: The union stays. ChartChangeRequest.ops remains the discriminated union ChartOp (add, move, rename, merge, split) and is sent as anyOf of five closed objects, each with a one-value 'op' enum (library 3.5). No flat op class is built now. The one unverified assumption is that the real CLIs accept anyOf of objects, so three guards make it safe: (a) the connector degrades to its prompted path on a structured-output error (connectors 3.6) and the Router remembers the failure per schema sha for the rest of the process, so the cost is at most one wasted call per process; (b) ReplyParser validates the result with the same union either way; (c) default tests check the schema offline. Two fixes found by running a copy of J2's _clean on pydantic 2.14.2: a free-key dict becomes the object {additionalProperties:false, required:[]} that accepts no key, so SplitOp.move_children (dict[Target, Target]) is replaced by moves: [ChildMove]<=20 with ChildMove(child: Target, to: Target), and transport_schema raises 'transport_dict' for any free-key dict in a model-facing class. Live check that settles flat or union: tests/library/test_lib_live_transport.py::test_chart_change_request_native (marker live, SUTRA_LIVE=1) calls ClaudeConnector.call_json and CodexConnector.call_json 5 times each with transport_schema(ChartChangeRequest), a six-node chart and the request 'merge Leads into Quotes and add a Support team'. It passes when how == 'native' and the reply validates in at least 4 of 5 trials on each CLI. If it fails on either CLI, set CHART_OPS_TRANSPORT = 'flat' in org_chart.py and add ChartOpFlat (op plus optional fields; flat_to_ops raises bad_op on a missing or surplus field), about 60 lines owned by L2.
settlements.why: The union is the form that was prototyped (a 2.3 KB schema), has no converter and no null padding, and its failure is soft (the prompted path); a flat class adds a second representation to maintain for a risk that may not exist. The live check is cheap and decisive, and the owner can run it on request (D8).
settlements.rejected: Building the flat class now (a converter and nulls in strict mode for an unproven problem); grouping ops by type in separate lists (changes the ordered-ops semantics and the 300-step test); treating 'the prompted path' as the design (it is only the net).

settlements.topic: Function-node runtime: who turns engine events into atoms, where it lives, which tables hold them, which WPs build it
settlements.decision: The runtime is two modules, one per process, joined by one event contract. (1) The package sutra_app/engine/fnodes/ (new, engine section, WPs E6 and E7) runs inside the engine process. layer.py:FunctionNodeHooks subclasses EventHooks, is selected by SUTRA_HOOKS (default 'sutra_app.engine.fnodes.layer:factory' when it imports; SUTRA_NODES=off disables it; SUTRA_NODES=enforce is reserved and the factory raises ValueError), and turns the hook calls turn_started, call_finished, turn_finished, run_status and run_error into work-atom transitions with the library lifecycle (open_atom, close_atom, abandon_atom). checks.py runs the verify checks in code, declare.py builds the AtomDraft from the library FunctionSpecs, ids.py makes atom ids. Each transition becomes one 'atom' event in events.jsonl (fields in S2-models-07). (2) sutra_app/orchestrator/projector.py (ORCH-6) with AtomStore (ORCH-3) turns those events into rows in the server process, the only SQLite writer. Tables: atoms (one table, schema 'work-atom/0.3' for function atoms), atom_ledger, chat_messages (the atom cards, in the function node's own session), graph_nodes (the FunctionNode body with open_atom and atom_count), usage_ledger.atom_id. The library supplies data and pure functions: FunctionSpecs and its new seed file (WP L10), Atom and the lifecycle (L4), the five reply families (L5), FunctionNode (L6). Version 1 is observe-only: it never changes a J2 prompt, reply, route or outcome (system_addendum stays empty, the prompt goldens stay byte-identical); verify decides the atom's state, not the turn. Build order: L1; then L4, L6 and L2 in parallel; L5; L10; E0 (needs L1); E6; then ORCH-1, ORCH-3, ORCH-4, ORCH-5 and ORCH-6 (needs E6); E3 sets the default hooks; E7 proves a whole run; UI-6 reads it.
settlements.why: Turns are seen only inside the engine process, so 'declare before the work' and 'code runs the check' are possible only there; the server is the only SQLite writer (ORCH-D5), so it stores and does not decide; the diagram draws the five function cards inside the Department runtime band; a subpackage keeps the rest of the engine free of the library's Atom, node and spec models; no j2.py patch is needed because P8 already exposes the hooks.
settlements.rejected: Deriving atoms on the server from say, usage and trace.jsonl lines (an atom would open after its work, the server would depend on J2 file formats, and enforcement could never move into the turn); putting the layer in the library (it does I/O and reads a clock), in the orchestrator (it cannot see turns) or in j2.py (P8 diff budget); a new top-level package; one atom per model call; enforcing from day one.

settlements.topic: Function-node atom lifecycle: grain, declaration, attempts, checks, observe mode
settlements.decision: Grain: one work atom per function turn (TurnInfo), not per model call; the turn's model calls are its attempts, and planner and judge calls are charged to the atom. Only the five function names open function atoms; builders W-n, the code validator, the judge and the reviewer do not (builders keep J2's atom/1). Declare (declare.py): pick the AtomTemplate by (function, TurnInfo.kind) from FunctionSpecs, else the function's template named 'generic'; goal = the template goal with {function} {kind} {step_label} {task} filled (an observable outcome, never a banal word); constraints = the first 20 of FunctionSpec.may_not as Constraint(text, check=None), as the plugin does; context = the TurnInfo.context pairs rendered '<kind>: <summary>' (<=200 characters, <=40 items); work = Work(dispatch_kind 'llm', agent = the function, steps = step_label, how_kind 'AI'), or ('bash', 'code') when the turn makes no model call; verify = the template's checks. Open: open_atom(...) before the first call; an open-time refusal is stored, ledgered and carded and the turn goes on (observe). Attempts: after each call_finished of the turn's own function with purpose 'agent_turn' while the atom is open, the runner executes the checks and close_atom is called; exit 0 closes (closed_by 'verify'); non-zero keeps the atom open with attempt+1 and a VERIFY FAILED card; at most 3 attempts. turn_finished: if the atom is still open, abandon_atom with a reason ('the check did not pass after N attempts: <first violation>' or 'the turn ended without a passing reply'); a turn without any agent_turn call is closed once with the check turn-posted. Run end (run_status waiting and not paused, run_error, SIGTERM): abandon every open atom with reason 'run ended: <status>'; a new turn_started first abandons a stale open atom of the same node. Version 1 check set: 'reply-valid' (args [family, kind], kind may list alternatives joined by '|': the call's reply parses and validates in the library family and kind through ReplyParser; evidence is 'ok' or the violation text) and 'turn-posted' (the turn posted a message or saved a record). Exit codes: 0 pass, 1 fail, 127 unknown template. The runner is pure Python in the run folder: no subprocess, no network, under 50 ms. J2's own recovery (re-asks, code repair) runs unchanged and only produces more attempts. Not in v1: write-scope enforcement (FunctionSpec.writes is recorded, not enforced), J2's named code checks as atom checks (charter stamp, workable, rate-card price and the like), enforce mode, builder atoms.
settlements.why: The plugin atom is one unit of work with a check declared before the work and run by code at close; a J2 function turn is that unit (the engine hooks, ORCH-D10 and the UI all say 'work atom per turn'). Attempts map onto J2's own re-asks, so J2 behaviour is unchanged (D4 b). reply-valid reuses the closed reply classes that already encode J2's role rules (REFUSE funds nothing, a PASS row needs evidence, order ids are unique), so verify has teeth without new J2 logic. Two templates keep version 1 small and testable offline.
settlements.rejected: One atom per model call (J2 turns make planner and judge calls that are not steps); hard write scope and J2's named code checks as atom checks in v1 (they need j2.py patches or state the hooks cannot see); blocking or retrying turns in v1 (changes J2 behaviour); a shell-based check runner with the plugin's 30 second alarm (pure checks need no subprocess); node state derived from atoms (the J2 lanes already give it).

settlements.decision: Event contract (extends ORCH 5.6 and ENG 4.5 together; one definition, the RunEvent union in orchestrator/models.py, plus an unconditional contract test). The 'atom' event keeps node and atom{id, schema, goal, work_kind, verify_template, status, attempt, closed_by, reason, body, ts_open, ts_closed} for J2 views (schema 'atom/1', unchanged). For function atoms schema is 'work-atom/0.3', status is the stored state (open, closed, refused, abandoned), body is the Checked[Atom] JSON as an object, ts_open and ts_closed are epoch seconds, and three new optional fields appear only for that schema: outcome (opened, verify_failed, closed, refused, abandoned), card (library Card: label, goal, rows[{label,text}]) and ledger (library LedgerRow, null while the atom stays open). The 'usage' event gains optional atom (the function atom id, or the workflow atom id for a builder call), stored in the new column usage_ledger.atom_id (indexed where not null). Tables: atoms stays one table with a per-schema state check ((schema 'work-atom/0.3' and state in open, closed, refused, abandoned) or (schema 'atom/1' and state in open, closed, verify_failed, abandoned)) and the unique index one_open_atom_per_node unchanged; atom_ledger gets a unique index on atom_id (one terminal row per atom); the card is a chat_messages row of kind 'card' in the function node's own session with card {type 'atom', atom_id, outcome, label, goal, rows} and src_ref '<run_id>#atom:<atom_id>:<outcome>:<attempt>'; the function node body takes open_atom and atom_count in the same transaction. Projector rules: gate the body (GATE.check 'atom'), accept only forward moves (none to open or refused; open to open with attempt+1, to closed or to abandoned; closed, abandoned and refused are final), append the ledger row when present, post the card, put_node, emit atom.updated; run.ended and reconcile abandon every still-open function atom of the run (abandon_atom, reason 'run ended: <status>'). Contract test: tests/engine/test_engine_events_contract.py (E7) imports sutra_app.orchestrator.models.RunEvent unconditionally and validates every builder output and the golden file tests/engine/golden/run_events.jsonl.
settlements.why: One definition of the event keeps the closed union safe for the watcher. Per-schema state checks keep each vocabulary honest inside one table, so /api/atoms has one read path. settlements.decision: AtomId keeps both forms in one pattern and each form names one class of atom: 'a-<sid>-<nn>' is a function-node atom (library Atom record, schema work-atom/0.3), 'W-<n>.a<k>' is a J2 workflow atom (J2 dict plus the atom/1 view). Two helpers in library types.py are the only code that builds a function atom id: atom_sid(run_id, node_id) = the first 10 hex digits of sha1('<run_id>:<node_id>') and function_atom_id(sid, n) = 'a-' + sid + '-' + n with at least two digits (checked: they match the AtomId pattern). n counts per (run, node) from 1 and every open attempt consumes a number, a refused one too, so gaps are normal. Atom.session_id holds the sid. J2 restarts workflow ids at W-1 in every run, so 'W-3.a1' is unique only inside a run: in the orchestrator the stored key of an atom/1 row (atoms.id, usage_ledger.atom_id, AtomOut.id) is '<run_id>:<atom/1 id>', for example 'j2-20261104-100004-7f3a:W-3.a1'; the atom/1 body keeps J2's id. settlements.topic: Chat links on a chart merge or split: archived sessions under a node
settlements.decision: The rule is the library's carry_links (pure) and the executor is the orchestrator's ChatStore.apply_links(tx, plan, names), which replaces ChatStore.archive. Every live node has exactly one active session, so in the app the outcomes are keep (the survivor) and archive (each merged-away node); move exists for completeness and is tested with a link map that lacks the target. Merge of sources S into target T: the session of each S becomes status 'archived', writable 0, note 'Merged into <T name>' and filed_under = T (its node_id stays the origin node id, so a division's filtered view of its scoped task lines keeps working); T's own session stays active and gets the note 'Took in <S name>'; sessions already archived under S are re-filed to T (resolve_alias); the graph node of S is deleted and the steps whose parent was S are re-parented to T; org_nodes keeps S as a retired row. Split: the node keeps its session, each new part gets a node and a session through ensure_node, moved children keep theirs, nothing is archived. Schema: chat_sessions.node_id is no longer UNIQUE and has no foreign key (history rows keep an origin id after the node is deleted); uniqueness is a partial index on active sessions; filed_under TEXT NULL is new; invariant I1 reads 'every graph node has exactly one active session and chat_session_id equals it'. NodeDetail gains archived_chats (sessions with filed_under = the node); GET /api/chats takes node_id and include=archived. No session is ever dropped.
settlements.why: One owner for the rule (library) and one for the execution (the chat store). Filing under the survivor is what LinkPlan.archive says (a session to a target node), so the library is executed literally. Keeping the origin node id keeps the division view correct, and deleting the retired graph node keeps the graph a view of live structure (no archived node state, check_graph needs no filter).
settlements.rejected: Archiving in place on a kept graph node with a state 'archived' (needs a node state J2 does not have and a filter in every graph read); re-pointing node_id to the survivor (the filtered division view would use the wrong scope); dropping archived sessions; leaving the rule in the orchestrator.

settlements.topic: Artifact models, rules, template bases and shared helpers: one definition owner, parity gate, import directions
settlements.decision: The library is the owner of the definitions: artifact section and document models, rules (RuleSpec), template bases and pure checks, certainty_zone, extract_json and close_json. For the artifact models, the rules and the template bases the engine keeps its vendored J2 files (j2_artifact_models.py, j2_rules.py, j2_template_lib.py, and certainty_zone inside j2_realization.py) as the runtime copy, because they define J2 behaviour (lax coercion, ENG-01) and are not edited. A drift test in the library, tests/library/test_lib_engine_parity.py (WP L8, skipped when sutra_app.engine is not importable), must stay green: per artifact model the transport_schema sha equals the engine's after the three declared library changes (const as enum, anyOf, no recursion); the valid/invalid verdict agrees on the shared corpus except the entries of tests/library/parity_allowlist.json (for example required: 'true'); run_rules gives identical results on every RULES entry; certainty_zone agrees on all signal combinations; extract_json and close_json are the same objects in engine.llm and connectors.jsonio.
